title: Create a Books Table
statement:
Create the table a small library keeps its books in.

The database starts empty. Create a table named `books` with these columns, in this order:

- `id`: an `integer` identity column that is the primary key, so PostgreSQL numbers the books 1, 2, 3 for you
- `title`: `text`
- `author`: `text`
- `published_year`: `integer`
- `in_stock`: `boolean` that is `true` when an insert leaves it out

Add no other constraints and do not name the primary key, so PostgreSQL names it itself. The starter already inserts three books, giving only their title, author, and year, and selects every column ordered by `id`. Then it shows how PostgreSQL describes each column and lists every constraint on the table. In the constraint list, `p` is a primary key and `n` is not null. Your table has to fill in `id` and `in_stock` on its own.

Expected output:

```text
CREATE TABLE

INSERT 0 3

 id |           title           |      author       | published_year | in_stock
----+---------------------------+-------------------+----------------+----------
  1 | The Left Hand of Darkness | Ursula K. Le Guin |           1969 | t
  2 | Things Fall Apart         | Chinua Achebe     |           1958 | t
  3 | Kindred                   | Octavia E. Butler |           1979 | t
(3 rows)

  column_name   | data_type | is_identity | column_default
----------------+-----------+-------------+----------------
 id             | integer   | YES         |
 title          | text      | NO          |
 author         | text      | NO          |
 published_year | integer   | NO          |
 in_stock       | boolean   | NO          | true
(5 rows)

  constraint_name  | type
-------------------+------
 books_id_not_null | n
 books_pkey        | p
(2 rows)
```

hints: `GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY` after a column's type makes PostgreSQL number the rows for you.
`DEFAULT true` after a column's type is the value an insert gets when it leaves that column out.

sql.starter:
CREATE TABLE books (
  id integer,  -- TODO: make id an identity column and the primary key
  title text,
  author text,
  published_year integer,
  in_stock boolean  -- TODO: default to true
);

INSERT INTO books (title, author, published_year) VALUES
  ('The Left Hand of Darkness', 'Ursula K. Le Guin', 1969),
  ('Things Fall Apart', 'Chinua Achebe', 1958),
  ('Kindred', 'Octavia E. Butler', 1979);

SELECT id, title, author, published_year, in_stock
FROM books
ORDER BY id;

-- How PostgreSQL describes each column
SELECT column_name, data_type, is_identity, column_default
FROM information_schema.columns
WHERE table_name = 'books'
ORDER BY ordinal_position;

-- Every constraint on the table, by the name PostgreSQL gave it
SELECT conname AS constraint_name, contype AS type
FROM pg_constraint
WHERE conrelid = 'books'::regclass
ORDER BY constraint_name;
sql.solution:
CREATE TABLE books (
  id integer GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  title text,
  author text,
  published_year integer,
  in_stock boolean DEFAULT true
);

INSERT INTO books (title, author, published_year) VALUES
  ('The Left Hand of Darkness', 'Ursula K. Le Guin', 1969),
  ('Things Fall Apart', 'Chinua Achebe', 1958),
  ('Kindred', 'Octavia E. Butler', 1979);

SELECT id, title, author, published_year, in_stock
FROM books
ORDER BY id;

-- How PostgreSQL describes each column
SELECT column_name, data_type, is_identity, column_default
FROM information_schema.columns
WHERE table_name = 'books'
ORDER BY ordinal_position;

-- Every constraint on the table, by the name PostgreSQL gave it
SELECT conname AS constraint_name, contype AS type
FROM pg_constraint
WHERE conrelid = 'books'::regclass
ORDER BY constraint_name;
